title: Lecture 7 · The Paxos protocol
outline: STATUS: complete. Lecture 7 video (Data Science, COM3021): 'The Paxos protocol', sub line 'How nodes agree with only a majority'. 11 scenes, about 122 s: title (4), why Paxos (10), three roles (11), proposal numbers (11), quorum (11.5), phase 1 prepare and promise (13), phase 2 accept (13), two proposers (14), safety (13), a log of rounds (12.5), recap (9). Story in the lessons' order: ds7-roles 7.1 (Paxos needs only a majority, proposers, acceptors, learners, unique increasing numbers, quorum of 3 of 5, any two majorities overlap) and ds7-rounds 7.2 (PREPARE and PROMISE, ACCEPT and ACCEPTED, learners after a majority, collisions, re-proposing an already accepted value, a log with one round per entry), workshop ds7-lab 7.W. Lessons: js/content/ds/ds-l7-01.js, ds-l7-02.js. All numbers are computed by a tiny Paxos simulation and asserted in videos/d7/common.js (D7).

titleCard.title: The Paxos protocol
titleCard.sub: How nodes agree with only a majority

title: Two-phase commit
needs everyone
caps: Two-phase commit needs all five to say yes.
One crash and it is stuck waiting.
scenes.spec: WHY PAXOS: two-phase commit (lecture 6) needs a yes from all five nodes, so one crash stalls it; Paxos needs a majority, 3 of 5, so two may crash. Data: D7.QUORUM.

title: Proposers suggest,
acceptors decide
caps: A node can play three roles.
Acceptors decide which one is chosen.
Learners are only told the result.
scenes.spec: THREE ROLES: a proposer suggests a value, five acceptors decide which one is chosen, learners are told the result (lesson 7.1). The value 7 flows through the three panels; the acceptors turn green. Data: D7.ACCS, D7.R1.v.

title: Every proposal has a
bigger number
caps: Each proposal gets a unique number.
The newer proposal beats the older.
scenes.spec: PROPOSAL NUMBERS: unique and increasing; proposer 1 uses 1, 3, 5, proposer 2 uses 2, 4, 6; a bigger number is newer and wins (lesson 7.1). The tags 'older' and 'newer: wins' mark 5 and 6.

title: A majority is
enough
caps: A majority of 5 is 3: a quorum.
They share at least one acceptor.
scenes.spec: QUORUM: a majority of five is three, so two may crash; {A, B, C} and {C, D, E} are two majorities and share C, so any two majorities overlap (lesson 7.1). Data: D7.QUORUM (checked by brute force over every majority).

title: Prepare,
then promise
scenes.spec: PHASE 1: PREPARE 1 goes to A to E (E has crashed), A to D answer PROMISE and will ignore older proposals; three promises are a quorum (lesson 7.2). Data: D7.R1.

title: Accept, then
tell the learners
caps: A majority accepted: it is chosen.
scenes.spec: PHASE 2: ACCEPT 1, 7 goes to the acceptors that promised, A to D accept 7 and tell the learners with ACCEPTED; at the third one the value is chosen and the learners are told (lesson 7.2). Data: D7.R1.

title: The bigger number
wins
caps: P1 asks A, B, C to promise 1.
P2 asks B to E to promise 2.
B and C ignore the older number.
P2 has a majority: 9 is chosen.
scenes.spec: TWO PROPOSERS: P1 (number 1, value 7) prepares A, B, C; P2 (number 2, value 9) prepares B, C, D, E; B and C ignore P1's ACCEPT, P2 wins with four acceptances, P1 retries with number 3 (lesson 7.2). Data: D7.DUEL.

title: A chosen value
is never changed
caps: P1 crashed after A and B accepted 7.
P2 asks B, C, D to promise 2.
So P2 must send 7, not its own 9.
scenes.spec: SAFETY: P1 crashed after A and B accepted 7; P2 (number 2) wants 9, prepares B, C, D; B reports the 7 it accepted, so P2 must send 7 (lesson 7.2). Data: D7.SAFE.

title: One Paxos round
per log entry
caps: Each log entry is one Paxos round.
Every replica gets the same order.
scenes.spec: A LOG OF ROUNDS: one Paxos round per log entry; round 1 chooses +50, round 2 chooses -20; three replicas hold the same entries in the same order and the balance goes 100, 150, 130 (lesson 7.2). Data: D7.LOG.

rows: A majority decides: 3 of 5, two may crash
Never change a value that may be chosen

helpers: videos/d7/common.js (D7): the simulation (D7.prepare, D7.accept, D7.pick), the asserted examples (D7.QUORUM, D7.R1, D7.DUEL, D7.SAFE, D7.LOG) and the rig D7.rig (proposers on the left, five acceptor cards in the middle, learners on the right). Drawing pieces come from d4/common*.js (VID.d4) and l5/common.js (VID.l5). Colour roles: blue = a proposer and its value, purple = protocol messages and numbers, green = promised, accepted, chosen, orange = older or abandoned, red = crashed or ignored, grey = neutral.
